title: Make the .secrets.baseline route guard detect a present-but-inert invocation, not merely a present substring
rebase_note: Originally cut from 8d525dbe7fe94d755a26e631b9869e0b3bfbfc31, which is the base every measurement in premise_predictions_stated_before_measurement was taken against. main moved to 80c1684 (PR #68, Google Cloud provider) mid-slice and this branch was rebased onto it. progress.md was resolved by taking main's blob verbatim and re-appending; .secrets.baseline did not conflict because this slice never touched it, so #68's growth from 21 to 31 tracked files and 75 to 107 entries is preserved. Every gate and the twelve route cases were re-measured against the new base. REBASED AGAIN onto 0b3dbde (PR #70, the AWS provider) AFTER the Level-2 evaluation PASSED on 30591fe. The rebase touched the two ledger files ONLY: tests/support/source_scan.py and tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py came through byte-identical, blobs 3a86f03a and 183619e0, verified by git hash-object rather than predicted. That is what keeps the completed evaluation composable: a ledger-only rebase leaves the artefact under review unchanged, while any source edit would invalidate it regardless of size. Two non-blocking findings (an empty path rendering for a root-level scalar, and a stale 3-tuple annotation on invocation_problems left over from the arity commit) are deliberately NOT fixed here for that reason, and are filed as follow-ups.
objective: tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py::test_every_route_invokes_the_validator asserts that four files still invoke the baseline validator, using a bare substring test: 'check_secrets_baseline' in text. A substring survives a comment character. The guard therefore constrains PRESENCE but not EFFECT, which is the same defect shape already found twice in this repository (a guard that asserted entries CHANGED without asserting HOW, and a fallback chain ending in a literal that always resolved). Replace the substring test with a check that extracts each file's EXECUTABLE content in that file's own language and asserts the invocation survives there, so a commented-out invocation is as red as a deleted one.
premise_predictions_stated_before_measur: P1 PREDICTED: on the untouched tree at 8d525db the route guard PASSES for all four files (positive control; a failure reported later means something only if this holds).
P2 PREDICTED: DELETING the invocation line makes the guard RED in all four of .github/workflows/ci.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/check.ps1, scripts/check.sh.

P3 PREDICTED: COMMENTING OUT the invocation line leaves the guard GREEN in all four, because a '#' prefix does not remove the substring. This is the defect. If measurement contradicts it, STOP and report rather than fixing what is not broken.

P4 PREDICTED: the four routes are three different languages (YAML, PowerShell, POSIX shell) plus shell nested inside YAML block scalars in ci.yml, so a single naive rule does not fit all four. ci.yml's invocation lives inside a 'run: |' block scalar, which is YAML data but shell CODE.

P5 PREDICTED: naive comment stripping (line.split('#')[0]) would corrupt real code in these files, because scripts/check.sh and ci.yml both contain ${#files[@]} / ${#FAILURES[@]} inside double quotes. Quote-aware scanning is therefore load-bearing, not decoration.

post_report_finding: THREE false positives, one cause, all found AFTER the slice was first reported complete - F by me probing read-only after standing down, FP-2 and FP-3 by the evaluator. F: an `args:` BLOCK sequence in .pre-commit-config.yaml was rejected though pre-commit executes it identically to the inline form. FP-2: an INLINE `run:` in the workflow was rejected; measured, ci.yml has 2 block-scalar and 16 inline `run:` keys, so the guard demanded the 2/18 minority spelling. FP-3: `entry: |` was rejected because the scanner marked entry content `shell` while that route's rule accepted only `yaml` - the two halves of the design contradicting each other. ROOT CAUSE: the YAML route rules asserted `context`, a LEXICAL property (which language's comment rules produced the line), as a proxy for executed position, a STRUCTURAL property (whether the text forms the value of a key the tool runs). A proxy fails in BOTH directions and each direction presents as a separate bug; my own diagnostic had been printing `context=yaml, key=run` all along. This is the slice's own thesis one level down - a lexical proxy cannot answer a structural question - so fixing it COMPLETES the slice rather than expanding it. FIX: route rules now assert OWNERSHIP, computed structurally from indentation and nesting rather than from spellings observed in these four files; `entry` removed from the shell-script key set because pre-commit shlex-splits and execs it rather than shell-interpreting it, making that treatment both unreachable and incorrect; non-script block scalars retained with their owning key rather than blanked, so prose is rejected for a reason instead of by invisibility. FIVE negative controls across both YAML routes (`name:` inline, `name: |`, `description: |`) stay RED throughout, so the widening is not a relaxation. A TypeError in the failure-message builder was caught by those controls on their first run.
parser_rebase: TEN defects were measured across the two hand-rolled revisions of the YAML half, in two families with one cause. FALSE NEGATIVES: `with: run:` (block and inline), `env: run:`, and a duplicate `entry:` overridden by a later one - all ACCEPTED though none executes. FALSE POSITIVES: CRLF files, both flow mappings, three alias shapes and a `<<:` merge - all REJECTED though every one is legitimate. Plus fail-OPEN as a class: a config too broken for PyYAML to load was certified as correctly wired. Root cause: hand-rolled line matching was standing in for a YAML parser, and each rework (lexical context, then nearest-key ownership, and next the key's start column) lost a round to a new spelling. FIX by composition: PyYAML resolves STRUCTURE, the existing shell scanner resolves the LEXICAL question inside a `run:` body; `.sh` and `.ps1` scanners untouched. Two load-bearing decisions. (1) WALK the schema rather than SEARCH it: selection consumes `jobs.*.steps[].run` and `repos[].hooks[].entry|args[]` segment by segment, so `with:` and `env:` are never visited and ancestry is enforced by construction - the rule never names `with`, because a rule spelled 'not under with' would be fitted to the decoy in front of it. (2) `safe_load` rather than `compose`: the composer keeps line marks but preserves duplicate keys and does not expand `<<`, so a compose-based verdict accepts a file whose `entry:` is overridden later. safe_load semantics ARE what the tools execute. Cost, stated not buried: line numbers are lost; diagnostics name the schema PATH instead, which says why a position is not executed rather than only where it sits. Fail-closed had to be BUILT: yaml.YAMLError is caught explicitly, pinned by four unparseable shapes that each carry the needle at a real `entry:` with an intact-document control in the same test. No new dependency: pyyaml==6.0.3 is a declared [project] dependency installed by CI's `pip install -e ".[dev]"` - verified, since the earlier claim that it came from apps/api/requirements.txt would not have held.
arity_finding: A FOURTH defect family, found by scoring falsifiable predictions I volunteered after standing down. `run:` written as a SEQUENCE was ACCEPTED although GitHub Actions types `run` as a string and such a workflow does not load at all; measuring the mirrors found two more that had not been reported, `entry:` as a sequence and `args:` as a scalar. One cause: the rule recorded whether a value is a shell script but not whether it is SCALAR- or LIST-valued, so terminal sequences were iterated unconditionally - right for `args`, wrong for `run` and `entry`. FIXED as arity rather than as the one reported shape: each pattern now carries (path, is_shell_script, is_list_valued), and selection distinguishes an intermediate sequence (steps, repos, hooks - always traversed) from a terminal one (accepted only where the schema says list). Fixed rather than disclosed because it is the SAME CLASS as the fail-open case fixed one commit earlier - an invalid config certified as correctly wired - and that fix was argued on the explicit ground that 'it fails loudly when the tool runs' is not sufficient; disclosing this while having just fixed the identical class would be incoherent. It is also a false NEGATIVE, the silent kind. Five wrong-shape cases and two paired right-shape controls are permanent tests. Separately, one DOCUMENTED and unrepairable limit is now pinned: PyYAML implements YAML 1.1, so a workflow's bare `on:` key parses as boolean True and a mention under it is reported at a path beginning `True.`; the verdict is unaffected, and the loaded document cannot say whether the source spelled it `on`, `yes` or `true`, so guessing a spelling back would invent information the parser discarded. Finally, the residual risk previously named as structurally invisible - whether either tool has an executed position the patterns miss - was closed from OUTSIDE the implementation by reading both schemas: pre-commit's hook definition carries exactly two command-bearing fields (entry, args) with all other keys metadata and all three repo kinds sharing that definition, and in a workflow jobs.<id>.steps[].run is the only key that executes a command. Recorded as strong corroboration rather than proof, since the pre-commit schema consulted is community-maintained.
typed_segments_and_honest_reasons: FOUR further findings from an independent evaluator, all verdicts previously correct but the EXPLANATIONS wrong and the intermediate type direction untouched. F4 (must-fix): two rejection branches asserted causes they had not established, and the flagship mode was the one they got wrong - commenting the invocation out of the real ci.yml reported 'appears at jobs.secrets.steps.[3].run, and none of those is a position this tool executes', naming a path that MATCHES the pattern the sentence says is unmatched. Same class as a coverage overclaim, one level down: there the guard claimed coverage it lacked, here a reason it had not shown. Fixed by establishing each reason from data already computed - needle present in an executed run: value but gone after shell-stripping means COMMENTED OUT; needle in raw text but absent from the loaded document is a YAML comment or a duplicate-key override, separated by consulting compose, which preserves duplicates; a live value at a non-executed path is named with its path. Four causes, four distinct messages, asserted distinct by test. F1 (general form): the previous arity fix asked 'may this KEY hold a list?', a property of the key checked once at the leaf, which left the intermediate direction open - steps: as a mapping, jobs: as a list, and repos:/hooks:/steps: as lists OF LISTS were all accepted, because a list of lists satisfies 'is a list' at every step while never being a list of mappings. Segments now carry their type and a sequence segment is iterated exactly once, after which the element must be whatever the next segment demands. Also corrected an evaluator measurement that was right for the wrong reason: steps: as a mapping rejected on the previous head only because `run` was not a DIRECT key; `steps: {run: ...}` was ACCEPTED there. Incidental protection again. F2: safe_load replaces safe_load_all because each tool reads ONE document; measured that safe_load raises ComposerError on a multi-document stream, and the message now names that case specifically. F3: a recursive alias crashed the diagnostics walk, which runs only while building a rejection, so the guard died exactly when explaining a failure; a cycle guard closes the instance and wrapping the whole explanation closes the CLASS - any exception still yields a rejection stating what is known, proven by a test that forces an unrelated exception. Deliberately NOT over-corrected: three shapes that already rejected correctly are now regression controls, and eight accept spellings most exposed to the new control flow still accept. 16/16 with zero mismatches. compose is diagnostics-only and that boundary is asserted, not merely honoured.
acceptance_criteria: A1 COMMENT-OUT IS RED: for each of the four route files, commenting out the invocation in that file's own comment syntax makes the guard fail.
A2 DELETION STAYS RED: for each of the four, deleting the invocation still makes the guard fail. The existing property must not be traded away for the new one.
A3 UNTOUCHED PASSES: each unmodified route file still passes. A false positive here teaches people to delete the guard, which is worse than the gap being closed.

A4 DESIGNED FROM THE PROPERTY, NOT THE INCIDENT: the check reasons about each file's actual comment syntax and executable regions, not a regex tuned to the one bypass in the brief. Quote-aware, here-doc/here-string aware, block-comment aware.

A5 LIMITS DECLARED: the present-but-inert modes considered are enumerated in the test module, split into caught and knowingly-not-caught. A guard whose limits are documented beats one whose limits are discovered later.

A6 PERMANENT, NOT ONE-OFF: delete and comment-out are asserted by tests operating on in-memory copies of the real files, so the property is re-measured on every run and needs no working-tree mutation.
A7 BYTE-EXACT RESTORE: any file mutated in the working tree for end-to-end measurement is restored byte-exactly, proved by git hash-object against git rev-parse ref:path, never numstat.
A8 NO CONTROL WEAKENED, NO TEST LOST: collected test count does not fall; no existing assertion is deleted or loosened.
A9 PROTECTED STATE: feature_list.json byte-identical, F008 still passes:false, zero diff to every locked path, the four route files byte-identical to base, progress.md insertions-only.
A10: the pull request is opened as a DRAFT and is not merged.
verification_plan: Re-derive origin/main with git ls-remote before branching and again immediately before reporting.
Bootstrap the venv FIRST; a fresh worktree lacks one and missing tooling produces phantom failures that prove nothing.
Positive control BEFORE anything else: the route guard passes on the untouched tree.
State the prediction for all twelve cases (4 files x delete/comment-out/untouched) BEFORE measuring, and record every place the prediction was wrong.
Measure the OLD guard's behaviour on all twelve cases to confirm the defect exists exactly as briefed, then the NEW guard's behaviour on the same twelve.
Drive the twelve cases through a script rather than by hand, so the measurement is deterministic and repeatable.
Never read an exit code through a truncating pipeline; Select-Object -First N corrupts $LASTEXITCODE. Capture the code immediately, and confirm any alarming result by a second method.
Quote git ranges as "$base..HEAD" so PowerShell does not split at the dot; run any filtered git diff UNFILTERED first as a positive control.
Read the PR's job-level CI status directly rather than trusting any inherited baseline claim.
Open a draft PR and inspect its state with gh pr view.
negative_tests: Comment-out must be RED in all four routes, in each file's own comment syntax (# for YAML, PowerShell and shell; additionally <# #> block comments for PowerShell).
Deletion must remain RED in all four routes.
A deleted route FILE must be red with a clear message rather than an unhandled traceback.
The extractor must not treat ${#files[@]} or ${#FAILURES[@]} as a comment; a naive stripper does, and that would be a false positive on correct code.
The extractor must not treat a '#' inside a quoted string as a comment.
An unconditional top-level early exit placed before the invocation must be RED for the shell-family routes.
data_implications: No migration, no schema change, no persisted state. Test-support code and tests only.
security_privacy: No network access, no credential material. The slice strengthens a guard that keeps a secret-scanning gate wired into all four routes; it does not touch the scanner or its exit-code handling.
portability: Standard library only; no new dependency and no YAML parser, so the guard cannot fail open or fail red because a parser is missing from an environment. Windows and POSIX both exercised: the extractor is pure text processing over bytes decoded as UTF-8.
z0_risk: Indirect but real. This guard is one of the mechanisms that keeps a secret-detection gate attached to every route into main. If it can be silenced by a '#', the gate can be silenced by a '#', and a leaked credential in a published evidence artefact is a far worse outcome than any classification error. No Z0 classification, quota calculation, or provider evidence is touched by this slice.
